state:
Goal `core-xml-writer`: `attribute`, `comment`, `cdata`, `instruction`, `doctype`, `content`, `startElement` and `endElement` of `Core\Xml\Writer` have all their feature proofs, and their cards in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/xml.rs` are in plain words.
`forbidden` now refuses U+FFFE and U+FFFF, in every writer and in the parser. `tests/conformance/core/xml-u-fffe-and-u-ffff-are-refused-by-every-writer-and-by-the-parser.nvst` pins that.
`startDocument` and `endDocument` still owe about.md, examples, hostile, perf and a Rust test. After them, `dossier-core-xml-writer` should be green.
Gap `nvs-stdlib/an-xml-writer-holds-a-string-per-piece` still stands: keep writer attacks and benches under about 500,000 pieces, or mark them with that gap.
Any later edit to `xml.rs` code makes the whole `Core\Xml*` perf set stale again. Finish with `bun nv proofs --record-perf --group 'Core\Xml' --group 'Core\Xml\Node' --group 'Core\Xml\Reader' --group 'Core\Xml\Writer'`.
`bun nv try` and `--bless` use the pipeline's `covws` binary. After a Rust change, run `cargo build --bin nvs` and set `NVS_BIN=target/debug/nvs.exe`.

backlog: `forbidden` refuses U+007F to U+009F, which XML 1.0 allows in a document. PHP's parser reads them. This is a correctness divergence, and it is not a security problem. It is owed by `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/xml.rs`'s module doc, if a later goal decides to allow them.
